data.why: The repository's own example data (data/merox, data/_fasta, data/pyxlms) bundles real crosslink search-engine output for the same reference dataset (Cas9 crosslinked with DSS). The MS Annika/pLink/Scout equivalents of this dataset are 150-350KB each so a representative row subset of the MeroX CSV was taken (same columns/values, same engine, same experiment) and copied verbatim in content; the FASTA and pyXLMS custom-format CSM/crosslink files are copied unmodified.

goals: Upload crosslink-spectrum-match (CSM) results from a search engine (e.g. MS Annika) and parse them with the correct crosslinker to get a readable CSM table and summary statistics
Filter and validate the parsed CSMs by target/decoy FDR estimation so only confidently identified crosslinks remain
Aggregate CSMs into unique crosslinks/residue pairs and inspect intra vs inter-protein crosslink counts
Upload a FASTA file to (re-)annotate crosslink positions onto a protein sequence
Filter crosslinks down to a protein of interest and visualize crosslink score/type distributions
Export validated crosslinks to a downstream structural-biology tool format such as PyXlinkViewer (PyMOL) or xiNET for mapping crosslinks onto a protein structure

review.summary: The tree follows pyXLMS's stated pipeline well (parse search-engine output → validate/aggregate → filter → plot → export), with clean general labels and screens that mostly match. But the structure-mapping handoff named in its own goal never succeeded, and FDR validation and the xiFDR export were shown only on toy or decoy-free data, so those central claims need fixing or re-scoping before filing.
